captures.notes: The first route surface is continuous, but it is a dark isolated strip beside lawn; the market frontage and a bounded urban alley do not read from the entrance.
This frame exposes a long open lawn sightline between separated building masses; neither a market bend nor dense frontage encloses the turn.
The occupied bridge is legible above, but the lower route opens directly to the horizon and the stairs do not form a facade-bounded vertical street.
A support wall fills most of the frame. The automatic ray probe also classifies the target as obscured, so this capture cannot verify the named alley.
The internal stair-house exists and climbs two storeys, but the opposing flights visually intersect without a distinct collision-bearing intermediate landing or readable guard openings.
The passage facade and doorway are visible, but they dominate the frame; the image does not establish the court as a shared local-ground space serving multiple onward relationships.
The target is ray-obscured by close massing and the rectangular harness rock stacks still substitute for a real uneven terrain payload, so the support relationship is not cleanly proven.
The structural court floor is complete and the exposed edge has continuous derived upper/lower rails and posts; adjoining building edges and the doorway side remain open.

The high passage floor and exterior doorway are present, but the descending route is small and distant through the opening; a sequential traversal proof is still needed to establish the continuous return.
The lower return passage has a complete facade, roof, doorway, rock perch, and continuous claimed floor reaching the portal.
The full-rise stair, its upper landing, surrounding occupied masses, and an overhead inhabited link are all legible in one sectional view.
The court, guards, passage facades, and onward stair are visible, but the ray audit reports the authored target as obscured; this view cannot close the transition gate.
The camera is collision-clear but resolves to a close wall/window view and does not show the underside, supporting braces, or route beneath the intended inhabited overhang.
The secondary link's endpoint houses sit on separate rectangular perches with lawn between them; the enclosed link is visually lost and the composition reads as disconnected islands.
Most roof and gable closures are present, but the automatic target ray is obstructed and the frame cannot prove every exposed top boundary in the dense centre.
The central cluster now has substantial vertical overlap and a guarded high court, but adjacent clusters remain separated by lawn and the proof still uses synthetic rectangular terrain supports.
The overview diagnoses a compact stacked central mass, but also several disconnected satellite perches, long dark path strips across grass, and an isolated secondary skywalk composition.

findings.evidence: The automated audit measures frontage_ratio=0.0435, overhead_route_ratio=0.1081, through_sightline_count=916, and max_sightline_m=46.5. Full-resolution views agree: lawn and horizon remain visible through the core and satellite masses read independently.
findings.invariant: The compact-core itinerary must be bounded by occupied frontage, contain no through-core ray, keep tangent visibility at most 12 m, and visually read as one interlocked accretion from eye level.

findings.evidence: The stair-house flights visually cross in one open volume without a distinct intermediate landing; the later descent is topologically connected but not yet demonstrated by a sequential capsule traversal or a clear before/on/after image set.
findings.invariant: Every stair transition must have exact lower/upper landings, continuous collision and guards, and bidirectional capsule proof through the same portals claimed by the graph.

findings.evidence: The line-of-sight verifier reports six collision-clear but target-obscured authored cameras. Several frames show a near wall or support instead of the geometry named by the view.
findings.invariant: Every named verification recipe must visibly prove its target at full resolution; collision clearance alone is insufficient.

findings.evidence: Terrain-street patches render as nearly black rectangular strips under the review lighting and are surrounded by uncovered lawn. Surface closure exists structurally but does not yet read as a finished street material or urban ground.
findings.invariant: Solved surface boundaries must produce readable continuous street/court material without exposing accidental grass or looking like debug slabs.

findings.evidence: The harness derives rectangular rock stacks beneath every terrain-bearing footprint rather than committing the pinned runtime terrain field required by the spec.
findings.invariant: The fixed visual proof must use a real uneven terrain site or the exact runtime terrain payload for a pinned seed, not synthetic rectangular support slabs.

findings.evidence: The secondary enclosed link is accepted by sockets and ancestry, but its endpoint blocks remain visually separated on isolated perches and the link is not legible from its dedicated capture.
findings.invariant: A secondary enclosed link must close adjacency inside the same compact mass and visibly reconnect the public realm; it cannot read as a detached skywalk branch between islands.
